references.text: Shows how God was with Joseph and blessed him in Potiphar's house, which led to Potiphar entrusting everything he owned to Joseph.
Rachel is described with exactly the same Hebrew expression as Joseph: 'beautiful of form and beautiful to look at' – a clear literary parallel between mother and son.
The principle of faithfulness and entrusted responsibility, just as Joseph was entrusted with all that Potiphar owned.
Sarai is described as beautiful in appearance, a similar formulation used for women (and Joseph) in Genesis.
Proverbs emphasize that the one who is diligent and faithful will be entrusted with responsibility, just as Joseph was entrusted by Potiphar.
Thematic parallel about physical beauty triggering destinies: Joseph's leads to trial, Absalom's to rebellion.
Narrative connection: The same Joseph's responsibility for food develops from stewardship in Egypt to the salvation of his family.
Theological parallel: Both Josephs receive great responsibility from a ruler (Potiphar/Pilate) through the action 'to entrust'.
